periodicity.text: The light curve is dominated by a smooth sinusoid with period 0.12404 d (Lomb-Scargle power 0.47); the adopted 1.36450 d is 11.00 x that. The true period is more likely 0.12404 d (pulsation or spots) or 0.24807 d (contact binary), and the 'eclipses' may not be eclipses.

writeup: TIC 182343782 is an eclipsing binary star candidate with an orbital period of 1.3645 days. Automated analysis of TESS photometry detected a primary eclipse showing a dimming of 0.22%, with a strong signal-to-noise ratio of 55.8. No secondary eclipse was detected. Pixel-level image analysis confirmed the signal originates near the target location, though with a centroid offset of 8.1 arcsec and a difference-imaging peak signal-to-noise of 5.8. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a previously unreported object. The machine-learning screening model assigned it a score of 0.88, indicating high confidence in the detection. The candidate passed all data quality checks without flags.
